nodes.name: Electrodeposition of CoFe LDH
nodes.procedure: CoFe LDH nanosheets were loaded on Cu₂S electrode through electrodeposition strategy. Before electrodeposition experiments, 0.072 mol Co(NO₃)₂ and 0.048 mol Fe(NO₃)₃ were dissolved in 20 mL deionized water as deposition solution. Then electrodeposition process was performed in above solution at 1.0 V versus Ag/AgCl for 300 s. Different Co and Fe proportions of Cu₂S/CoFe LDH were synthesized by similar process, performing in deposition solution of different molar ratios for Co(NO₃)₂ and Fe(NO₃)₃, but total mole number was fixed to 0.12 mmol. Cu₂S/CoFe LDH electrode was rinsed with deionized water and ethanol, then dried in vacuum.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH (primary test)
nodes.source_text: The OER performance of as-prepared electrocatalysts was measured with a typical three-electrode system in oxygen-saturated 1M KOH aqueous solution... Cu2S/CoFeCuOOH delivers the ultralow overpotentials of 170 and 268mV to reach catalytic current densities of 10 and 100mAcm−2, respectively... Tafel slope of 41mVdec−1... The obtained Cdl value of Cu2S/CoFeCuOOH is 8.4mFcm−2... TOF value of 3.2 s−1 at overpotential of 300mV... No obvious decrease in current density could be observed after 100h... FE of 99.2%
Cu2S/CoFeCuOOH exhibits distinct pH-dependent kinetics... from the changes of current density at 1.5V versus RHE of pH value from 12.5 to 14... Cu2S/CoFeCuOOH has a much higher ρRHE (0.78)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFe LDH shows amorphous structure with Cu₂S peaks at 43.3°, 50.4°, 74.1° (111), (200), (220) planes; after activation Cu₂S peaks weaken but maintain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All XRD patterns (Figure S2, Supporting Information) display the same group of peaks at 43.3°, 50.4°, and 74.1°, which were attributed to (111), (200), and (220) planes of cubic-structured Cu ... From XRD pattern of Cu₂S/CoFe LDH after activation in Figure 2b, the peaks of Cu₂S phase maintain but exhibit tiny weakening.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFe LDH shows Cu₂S nanorods wrapped by dense CoFe LDH nanosheets (Figure S9); morphology maintains nanosheets-covered nanorods after activation (Figure 2c-f).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequently, Cu₂S nanorods were wrapped by dense CoFe LDH nanosheets after electrodeposition reaction (Figure S9, Supporting Information). The morphology of Cu₂S/CoFe LDH after activation manifests no distinct variation after CV treatment, maintaining the state of the nanosheets covered the nanorods (Figure 2c-f and Figures S14-S16, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFe LDH shows core-shell nanostructure of CoFe LDH nanosheets on Cu₂S nanorods (Figure S12); HR-TEM reveals amorphous-crystal phases with 0.26 nm fringe spacing assigned to Cu₂S (224) plane (Figure 2d).
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images confirm the core-shell nanostructure of Cu₂S/CoFe LDH (Figure S12, Supporting Information), presenting the typical morphology of CoFe LDH nanosheets decorated Cu₂S nanorods. Furthermore ... the combined structure with obvious amorphous-crystal phases for nanosheets-nanorods area can be detected by HR-TEM (Figure 2d), indicating that the fringe spacing of 0.26 nm could be assigned to (224) plane of Cu₂S.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFe LDH shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ (780.2/795.5, 781.5/796.9 eV), Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ (709.8/711.3, 718.6/724.3 eV), Cu⁺ (932.7/952.6 eV); after activation shows Co⁴⁺ (780.7/795.8 eV), increased Cu²⁺, oxygen vacancies at 531.8 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For pristine Cu₂S/CoFe LDH, the XPS peaks of Co 2p located at 780.2/795.5 and 781.5/796.9 eV could be attributed to Co³⁺ and Co²⁺ ... new peaks at 780.7 and 795.8 eV correspond to Co⁴⁺ species for Cu₂S/CoFe LDH after activation ... a new peak can be ascribed to oxygen-vacancies (Ov) of Cu₂S/CoFe LDH after activation at 531.8 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFe LDH shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ oxidation at 1.0 V (460 nm), Co³⁺/Co⁴⁺ at 1.2 V (565 nm); occurs at lower potentials than CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the applied potential up to 1.0 V versus RHE, a broad absorption band at ≈460 nm appeared for Cu₂S/CoFe LDH, corresponding to the oxidation process of Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ... Another new absorption band at ≈565 nm was visible at 1.2 V versus RHE and above for Cu₂S/CoFe LDH owing to the oxidation of Co³⁺ to Co⁴⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFe LDH transforms from Co₃O₄/CoOOH/Co(OH)₂ mixture to CoOOH at 0.9 V (Eg 508, A1g 590 cm⁻¹), then to CoO₂ at 1.2 V (470, 570 cm⁻¹) with Cu-O at 300 cm⁻¹; occurs at lower potentials than CoFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman peaks exhibit significant phase transformation at the applied potential of 0.9 V versus RHE for Cu₂S/CoFe LDH ... two new peaks located at 508 and 590 cm⁻¹ appeared, which can be indexed to Eg and A1g vibrational modes of Co-O for CoOOH ... these two Raman peaks stabilized at 470 and 570 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the Eg and A1g vibrational modes of CoO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH shows Co K-edge pre-edge at 7710 eV (CoO₆ octahedral), positive edge shift (>Co³⁺), Co-O at 1.43 Å, Co-O-M at 2.40 Å; Co-O coordination number <6 indicating oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH is characterized by a weak pre-edge peak at 7710 eV ... The absorption edge ... is positively shifted towards higher energy relative to CoOOH reference, manifesting an increased average valence state (more than 3+) of Co ... the peak at 1.43 Å is attributed to the first shell Co-O scattering ... the Co-O coordination number is significant lower than 6 due to the generation of oxygen vacancy (Ov).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH shows C_dl = 8.4 mF cm⁻², higher than CoFeOOH (3.9 mF cm⁻²), indicating higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained C_dl value of Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH is 8.4 mF cm⁻², much higher than CoFeOOH (3.9 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Co, Fe, Cu, O in nanosheets area and Cu, S in nanorods area for Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH after activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Cu₂S/CoFe LDH after activation, Co, Fe, Cu, and O are homogeneously distributed in nanosheets area while the Cu and S are distributed in nanorods area, corresponding to element mapping (Figure 2f and Figure S17, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH shows smallest charge transfer resistance R_ct compared to other electrocatalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) are shown in Figure 4h, Cu₂S/CoFeCuOOH exhibits the smallest charge transfer resistance (R_ct) in comparison to other electrocatalysts.
